claims.text: DFT combined with phonon-dispersion calculations can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed method will improve predictive accuracy by at least 15% relative to current predictions.
The target materials are polycrystalline high-entropy alloys.
The proposed predictions apply from 300 K to 1000 K under ambient pressure.
Phonon-dispersion relations and lattice dynamics mediate the relationship between the calculations and predicted thermal conductivity.
Ab initio calculations can determine phonon-phonon interactions and scattering rates in the target high-entropy alloys.
Phonon-phonon interactions and scattering rates determine phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed method will predict phonon thermal conductivity at least 15% lower than current predictions.
A current prediction of 5 W/m-K would be reduced to 4.25 W/m-K by the proposed method.
Current phonon thermal-conductivity predictions are based on empirical models or simplified theoretical approaches.
The method is applicable only to high-entropy alloys containing no more than five constituent elements.
The method is applicable only when the alloy has a mixing entropy of at least 1.5R.
Predictive accuracy may depend on the exchange-correlation functional.
Predictive accuracy may depend on pseudopotential quality.
Predictive accuracy may depend on convergence of the phonon-dispersion calculations.
TDTR experiments can provide the phonon thermal-conductivity values needed to benchmark the predictions at 300 K and 1000 K.
A deviation greater than 20% between measured and predicted phonon thermal conductivity is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
